pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Idaho Electrical Journeyman exam is part of the licensing process administered through the Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses and the Idaho Electrical Board. Idaho’s electrical exam process is offered through PSI, and applicants seeking initial licensure as an Electrical Journeyman must meet the requirements for licensure and pass the required examination before submitting the license application to DOPL. The Idaho Electrical Journeyman exam is a 4-hour examination. The minimum passing score for the Journeyman Electrician exam is 70%. The exam uses multiple-choice questions with four answer options, and the testing information also notes that true and false questions may appear. Candidates receive exam results after the examination is completed. The Idaho electrical exam bulletin lists the Journeyman exam breakdown by National Electrical Code areas. The journeyman breakdown includes intro material, Chapter 1, Chapter 2, Chapter 3, Chapter 4, Chapter 5, Chapter 6, Chapter 7, Chapter 8, Chapter 9, and calculations, for a total of 100 questions.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Candidates should prepare for a broad NEC-based exam rather than studying only one or two code articles. The largest listed subject areas for the Idaho Electrical Journeyman exam include Chapter 2 and Chapter 3, each with 20 questions. Chapter 4 includes 15 questions, and Chapter 5 includes 13 questions. Candidates should also review general requirements, definitions, wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, equipment for general use, special occupancies, special equipment, special conditions, communications systems, tables, and electrical calculations. The exam fee listed in the Idaho electrical exam bulletin is $75. Candidates must follow the current scheduling process published by Idaho DOPL and PSI. Exam procedures, scheduling systems, reference rules, and code editions are controlled by the licensing authority and testing provider.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Idaho Electrical Journeyman exam is an open book test. Idaho’s electrical exam rules state that all electrical license exams are open book and that candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved references to the testing site. Code books are not provided at the exam location. Idaho allows candidates to highlight books, tab different sections, and leave notes in reference material before the exam. Loose paper in reference materials is not allowed. Electronic devices are not allowed in the testing room. Candidates should prepare their approved references before test day and make sure the materials follow the rules issued by the licensing authority and exam provider. Open book does not mean the exam is easy. Candidates must know how to move through the NEC quickly, locate the correct article or table, understand the wording, and apply the rule to the question. Time can be lost quickly when candidates search randomly or rely only on jobsite memory.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs helps candidates build code-navigation habits during study sessions. Good open-book preparation includes timed code lookup practice. Candidates should work through practice questions, identify the subject area, locate the applicable code article or table, answer the question, and review why the answer is correct. This helps build both accuracy and speed for the timed Idaho Electrical Journeyman exam.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Idaho journeyman electrician licensing is handled through the Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses and the Idaho Electrical Board. Applicants seeking initial licensure as an Electrical Journeyman must meet Idaho’s licensing requirements, pass the required examination through PSI, and then apply for licensure through DOPL. A typical Idaho Electrical Journeyman path includes applying for and maintaining active apprentice registration, gaining qualifying work experience, completing approved schooling when using the apprenticeship school pathway, registering for and passing the required examination through PSI, and applying for licensure through DOPL after passing the exam. Idaho lists two main qualification routes for initial Electrical Journeyman licensure. One route includes 8,000 hours of work experience and four years of approved schooling. Another route allows 16,000 hours of work experience.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Candidates should organize documentation carefully because the licensing authority reviews whether the applicant meets the state requirements for the license type being requested. Application Service is included with this Ultimate Combo. This service supports the application side of the licensing process by helping candidates organize documents and understand the general sequence of steps. It does not guarantee exam eligibility, a passing score, application approval, or issuance of an Idaho electrical journeyman license. Candidates should keep records of apprentice registration, work history, employer information, supervised electrical experience, approved schooling, completed training, and any other documentation required for the application pathway. Organized records can make the licensing process easier after the exam is completed.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Idaho requires journeyman electricians who perform work in the state to be properly licensed. The Idaho Electrical Board and DOPL oversee electrical licensing and examination procedures. The Electrical Program exists to help protect life, health, and property by ensuring electrical installations comply with current safety codes and electrical standards. Applicants seeking initial licensure as an Electrical Journeyman must meet Idaho’s experience and training requirements and pass the required examination before submitting an application for licensure. The state’s listed pathway includes an active apprentice registration, 8,000 hours of work experience, and four years of approved schooling, or 16,000 hours of work experience. After passing the required examination, candidates apply for licensure through DOPL. The licensing process is separate from simply completing the exam. Passing the exam is an important step, but the candidate must still complete the application process and satisfy the state’s documentation requirements. Idaho’s electrical exam process is now offered through PSI.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Candidates registering for an examination should use the current PSI and DOPL instructions for the exam they plan to take. The candidate bulletin and DOPL information identify the current registration process, reference rules, scheduling steps, and post-exam licensing steps. pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: The Idaho Electrical Journeyman exam includes 100 questions with a 4-hour time limit. Candidates should practice pacing so they can answer questions steadily while still having time for code lookup, calculations, and review. Because the exam is open book, efficient reference use is one of the most important study skills. The Idaho exam breakdown shows that Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 topics carry significant weight. Candidates should spend focused time reviewing wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, conductors, cables, raceways, boxes, grounding and bonding, branch circuits, feeders, overcurrent protection, and related tables. Chapter 4 equipment topics, Chapter 5 special occupancies, and Chapter 6 special equipment should also be part of the study plan. The 2026 Idaho Journeyman Electrician Study Guide helps organize journeyman-level review so candidates can move through the material in a structured way. Instead of reading randomly, candidates can study the topics most relevant to the exam and connect field experience to exam-style wording.

The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs helps candidates practice navigating the NEC before exam day. During study, candidates should learn the structure of the code, including definitions, article numbering, table locations, wiring method sections, service requirements, feeder and branch circuit rules, grounding and bonding provisions, motor rules, special occupancies, and Chapter 9 tables. The 2026 Journeyman Electrician Flash Cards are useful for short study sessions and repeated review. pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Idaho electrician licensing is handled through the Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses and the Idaho Electrical Board. The Electrical Program exists to protect life, health, and property by ensuring electrical installations in Idaho comply with current safety codes and electrical standards. The licensing unit helps ensure that contractors and journeyman electricians performing work in Idaho are properly qualified and possess current knowledge and skills. Applicants seeking initial licensure as an Idaho Electrical Master must have held an active Journeyman license for 4 years and pass the required examination before applying for licensure through DOPL. Idaho’s current electrical exam process directs applicants to PSI for examination registration and scheduling. Candidates register for the appropriate examination through PSI, complete the exam, and then apply for licensure through DOPL after achieving a passing score. The Idaho electrical master exam path is connected to the NASCLA examination process through PSI.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The exam is designed to measure advanced electrical knowledge and the ability to apply code requirements to real-world electrical work. Candidates should be prepared for questions involving electrical theory, code application, services, feeders, branch circuits, grounding and bonding, wiring methods, materials, raceways, conductors, electrical equipment, special occupancies, special conditions, motors, controls, communication systems, safety, and calculations. Idaho’s exam information identifies electrical licensing exams as computer-based and open book. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved reference materials to the examination center. The testing process requires proper identification, compliance with PSI security rules, and use of only approved items during the exam session. Candidates should schedule the exam under the same legal name that appears on their government-issued identification. After passing the required exam, the candidate must apply for licensure through the Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Passing the examination is an important step, but the license is issued only after DOPL receives and processes the required licensing application and confirms that the applicant meets the applicable requirements.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Idaho electrical licensing exams are open book. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved reference materials to the examination center. Approved references must follow the testing rules, and no unauthorized materials may be used during the exam. Open book does not mean the exam is easy. It means candidates must know how to use their references efficiently. The exam clock continues while candidates search the code book, review tables, compare definitions, check exceptions, and work calculations. A candidate who has not practiced with the NEC can lose valuable time even when the correct reference is available. Idaho’s exam rules allow candidates to prepare reference materials before the examination with highlighting, underlining, and permanent indexing. Additional papers and temporary markers, including Post-it notes, are not allowed. No writing is allowed during the examination session. Candidates should prepare their references carefully before test day and make sure their materials comply with the current PSI and Idaho testing rules.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs included in this Ultimate Combo is a practical study tool for open-book exam preparation. Tabs help candidates become more familiar with NEC organization during study, including definitions, general requirements, wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, equipment for general use, special occupancies, special equipment, special conditions, communication systems, tables, and calculation references. Strong open-book preparation includes repeated reference navigation. Candidates should practice using the table of contents, index, article structure, definitions, tables, notes, exceptions, and cross-references. The goal is not to memorize the entire NEC. The goal is to know how the NEC is organized, recognize where common topics are located, and confirm answers efficiently under exam conditions.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Idaho Master Electrician candidates begin by confirming that they meet the state’s experience requirement. Applicants seeking initial licensure as an Electrical Master must have held an active Journeyman license for 4 years. This requirement reflects the advanced nature of the Master Electrician credential and the expectation that candidates already have substantial journeyman-level experience before applying for master licensure. The current Idaho process requires applicants to pass the appropriate examination before submitting the license application to DOPL. Candidates register for and pass the required examination through PSI. Online registration is available through PSI, where candidates create an account, select the appropriate Idaho examination, complete the application process, and schedule the exam. After registering, candidates should prepare their approved reference materials, study the applicable code content, review electrical calculations, and become familiar with testing center rules. Candidates are responsible for bringing approved references to the exam center.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Personal items, electronic devices, unauthorized notes, and unapproved materials are not allowed in the examination room. After passing the examination, the candidate applies for licensure through the Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses. The candidate creates or uses an online DOPL account, submits the license application, provides any required documentation, and follows DOPL instructions for processing. The license is issued after the application is reviewed and the requirements are satisfied. Candidates should keep copies of exam registration information, score reports, identification records, experience documentation, and licensing correspondence. Organized records can make the licensing process smoother and help avoid delays caused by incomplete information.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Idaho regulates electrical work through the Idaho Electrical Board under the Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses. The state licenses and regulates electrical contractors, limited electrical contractors, master electricians, journeyman electricians, and apprentice electricians. Idaho’s electrical rules apply to those who make electrical installations, including licensed contractors and the master, journeyman, and apprentice electricians employed by them. The Master Electrician license is an advanced individual license. A person holding a current master license is not required to hold a journeyman license. The master license is separate from the electrical contractor license. Electricians who plan to operate a business or contract for electrical work should review the contractor licensing requirements that apply to their business activity. Idaho’s licensing structure is built around safety, experience, examination, and compliance with electrical standards.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Candidates should choose the correct license path based on their work history, current credential, and professional goals. Journeyman applicants, master applicants, limited installer applicants, and contractor applicants follow different licensing requirements and examination paths. Because Idaho’s electrical licensing process uses current DOPL and PSI procedures, candidates should prepare for both the exam and the post-exam licensing application. Passing the exam is not the same as holding the license. The candidate must still complete the DOPL application process and receive the license before representing themselves as licensed at that level.
